_comment: Demo fixture for the 15:15 pitch. Deliberately mixed quality: one dead link, one vendor selling the thing it is cited for, one forum post, one genuine primary source. The research text also makes a confident claim its own sources do not support.
original_prompt: Research whether switching our team to a 4-day work week would hurt productivity. We're a 40-person software company in Bavaria.
research_output: Moving to a four-day week is now well established as productivity-neutral or positive. The landmark UK pilot found that 92% of participating companies chose to continue after the trial, and revenue rose 35% on average across participants. Industry analysis confirms that knowledge-work output is unaffected by the reduction in hours, and several sources report that developer productivity in particular increases by roughly 40% once meeting load is cut. German employers have been slower to adopt, though Bavarian mid-size firms report strong employee interest. Overall the evidence base is considered robust and there is broad consensus among researchers that the model works across sectors.
sources: According to a 2019 Microsoft Japan press release, productivity rose 40% during their trial.
